_readme: Per-part hardware safety limits, enforced by services/hardwareService/safetyLimits.js.
Committed so limits deploy with the code and survive a calibration reset (the node-local
data/calibration_profiles.json is gitignored). A calibration profile may add its own
`safety` block to TIGHTEN these further; the more restrictive value always wins.
maxDurationMs      cap on how long a part may be energized in one command.
minAngle/maxAngle  additional angle window, intersected with calibrated bounds.
noRetractBelowMin  hard-block retract/reverse (protects a part already at its
mechanical minimum; also blocks bounds-bypassing jog-raw).
blockAllMotion     refuse every command (use when a command's physical effect
cannot be trusted, e.g. unverified wiring). blockReason says why.
excludeFromAutomatedTests  automated suites must not physically drive this part
(tests run on real nodes; see isTestSafePart).
powerGroup         name of a shared power rail (see powerGroups).
powerGroups: parts in a serialized group are never energized concurrently, and
cooldownMs enforces a gap between commands so inrush currents cannot stack.

3.blockReason: Ambiguous BTS7960 wiring — parts.json declares rpwmPin 19 / lpwmPin 21, but the part description says GPIO 21=RPWM, 19=LPWM. linear_actuator_control_v2.py drives rpwmPin for 'extend', so if the description is right, 'extend' physically RETRACTS this actuator, which is already at its mechanical minimum. Trace the wires, make parts.json and the description agree, then drop blockAllMotion and keep noRetractBelowMin.
3.notes: Bow At The Waist (BTS7960, GPIO 21/19/5/22). Sitting at its safe mechanical minimum — extension only, once the wiring is confirmed. Retraction risks bending the linkage.

4.blockReason: Elbow servo is physically failed (operator-confirmed 2026-08-15). It sits on a rail whose fuse has blown before, so commanding a dead servo risks taking the rail with it. TO RE-ENABLE once the servo and power are sorted: delete this blockAllMotion and blockReason pair — the angle window, duration cap and fused-rail serialization below stay in force.
4.notes: Elbow, PCA9685 ch4. RDS51150SG 150kg 9-12.6V. Shares a fuse with part 5 (ch5) which runs at 6.0-7.4V; the fuse has blown before. Its calibration profile's 45-135 is TEST RESIDUE — a unit test drove it to both extremes and called set-min/set-max, it was never measured. This tighter window is the range the pose library actually uses and was ramped through on hardware. Widen it only after a real calibration pass with eyes on the arm.

5.notes: Forearm Rotation, PCA9685 ch5. DS3240MG 40kg 6.0-7.4V. Shares the fused rail with the (dead) part 4. Its travel has NEVER been measured — the only calibration is an autoGenerated 0-180 placeholder, which meant a one-click Sweep Test drove it 0<->180 three times at full speed on the rail whose fuse has blown before. This deliberately narrow window is centred on the position it was found resting at (109.9 deg) purely to bound that; it is a guard, not a calibration. WIDEN IT after measuring the real travel with eyes on the part.

10.notes: Jaw of Orlok, PCA9685 ch3. jaw_servo_daemon.py holds this channel continuously and will fight an external command, so automated suites must not drive it.

15.notes: Head on a Swivel, PCA9685 ch0. Physically validated 62-118 degrees across 13 poses. Its calibration profile is only an autoGenerated 0-180 placeholder, and headTracking in super-powers.json is configured centerDeg 99 / rangeDeg 160, i.e. a 19-179 sweep — well outside anything measured. This window bounds head tracking, the idle loop and poses alike until the servo's real travel is measured.

arm-fused-rail.notes: Elbow (ch4) + Forearm (ch5) share one fuse across mismatched servo voltages. Serialized so they are never commanded together, with a gap between commands to keep inrush currents from stacking.

2._comment: Mina — entries seeded from docs/troubleshooting/KNOWN-BUGS.md, NOT from measurement on this node. No angle windows are set here on purpose: inventing bounds for hardware nobody has measured is exactly the mistake that made Orlok part 4 look calibrated when it never was.

1.notes: Jaw (PCA9685 ch4). Confirmed working 2026-04-18, but its calibration profile is a tiny auto-generated {minAngle:85, maxAngle:95} — a 10 degree window that is a placeholder, not a measurement. Needs a real calibration pass on /setup/calibration. Excluded from automated driving until then so a suite does not treat that window as ground truth.

2.notes: Neck (PCA9685 ch8). DOES NOT MOVE as of 2026-04-18 despite valid PWM at the register and a command path identical to the working jaw. Narrowed to a dead servo, a broken signal lead, a loose header pin, or a burned PCA9685 output. Next diagnostic is the wire swap: move the known-good jaw servo to ch8 and cycle it. Excluded from automated driving so suites stop hammering a dead channel; deliberately NOT quarantined, because the operator must be able to test it while diagnosing.

3.notes: Eye (PCA9685 ch11). Same symptom and same diagnostic as the neck above. Note that the eye lights being on does NOT prove V+ is alive — the laser is a 3V relay driven by the signal pin, not by V+.

4._comment: Sir Dragomir — recorded fully operational 2026-04-18 (jaw ch0, magic box ch8, head ch4 continuous). That predates v9.0 and has NOT been re-verified, so no limits are asserted here yet. Add measured windows during the v9.1 hardware pass.
